fullPassage: One could say that judging or pre-judging is natural and necessary for protection and safety, but there are times that it just doesn't apply. There are an infinite number of examples and ways in which we judge daily, and we have to distinguish what type of judging we are doing. It's very easy to judge somebody else's choices, relationship, parenting style, condition of their home, finances, and everything else, but there's a reason for almost everything. If we look past the surface, we may see a deeper problem that warrants some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment on our part. I have judged people based on what they had on, where they lived, their accent, their financial status, or their behavior, but my perception and judgement didn't make it true. Now, I immediately check myself and say, "Girl, STOP!"

questions.stem: 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.question:
One could say that judging or pre-judging is natural and necessary for protection and safety.

(A) If we look past the surface, we may see a deeper problem that warrants some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment on our part.
(B) But there are times that it just doesn't apply, and we have to distinguish what type of judging we are doing.
(C) It's very easy to judge somebody else's choices, relationship, parenting style, condition of their home, finances, and everything else, but there's a reason for almost everything.
questions.analysis: 주어진 문장: 판단은 자연스럽다 → (B) 하지만 항상 적용되지 않음, 구별 필요 → (C) 판단하기 쉽지만 모든 것에 이유가 있다 → (A) 표면 너머를 보면 더 깊은 문제가 있다. (B)-(C)-(A) 순.

questions.stem: 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.question:
There are an infinite number of examples and ways in which we judge daily.

(A) Now, I immediately check myself and say, "Girl, STOP!"
(B) I have judged people based on what they had on, where they lived, their accent, their financial status, or their behavior, but my perception and judgement didn't make it true.
(C) We have to distinguish what type of judging we are doing — it is very easy to judge somebody else's choices.
questions.analysis: 일상의 판단 → (C) 구별이 필요, 타인의 선택 판단이 쉬움 → (B) 필자의 과거 판단 경험 → (A) 지금은 스스로를 점검. (C)-(B)-(A) 순.

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 위치를 고르시오.
questions.insertSentence: But there's a reason for almost everything if we look past the surface.
questions.question: ( ① ) One could say that judging or pre-judging is natural and necessary for protection and safety. ( ② ) There are an infinite number of examples and ways in which we judge daily, and we have to distinguish what type of judging we are doing. ( ③ ) It's very easy to judge somebody else's choices, relationship, parenting style, condition of their home, finances, and everything else. ( ④ ) We may see a deeper problem that warrants some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment. ( ⑤ ) Now, I immediately check myself.
questions.analysis: ③번 위치: '판단하기 쉽다' 다음에 '하지만 거의 모든 것에 이유가 있다'가 역접으로 연결되며 자연스럽다. 이후 ④에서 더 깊은 문제를 볼 수 있다는 내용으로 이어진다.

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 위치를 고르시오.
questions.insertSentence: My perception and judgement didn't make it true.
questions.question: ( ① ) One could say that judging or pre-judging is natural and necessary. ( ② ) We have to distinguish what type of judging we are doing. ( ③ ) If we look past the surface, we may see a deeper problem that warrants some understanding and empathy. ( ④ ) I have judged people based on what they had on, where they lived, their accent, their financial status, or their behavior. ( ⑤ ) Now, I immediately check myself and say, "Girl, STOP!"
questions.analysis: ④번 뒤: '나는 많은 것에 기반해 판단했다' 다음에 '하지만 나의 인식과 판단이 사실을 만들지는 않았다'로 자연스럽게 연결. ⑤번 앞에 역접으로 위치.

questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.question: There are an infinite number of examples and ways [in / we / which / judge / daily].
questions.analysis: 관계대명사 which + 전치사 in. 'ways in which we judge daily' 순서.

questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.question: If we look past the surface, we may see a deeper problem [warrants / that / some / understanding / empathy / or / even / enlightenment].
questions.wa: that warrants some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment
questions.analysis: 관계대명사 that절: that warrants some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment.

questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.question: One could say that ①judging or pre-judging is natural and necessary for protection and safety, but there are times that ②it just doesn't apply. There are an infinite number of examples and ③ways in which we judge daily, and we have to distinguish ④what type of judging we are doing. It's very easy ⑤judging somebody else's choices.
questions.analysis: ⑤ judging → to judge. 'It is easy to judge'에서 가주어-진주어 구문은 to부정사를 사용해야 한다.

questions.stem: 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현을 고르시오.
questions.question: I have judged people based on what they had on, where they lived, their accent, their financial status, or their behavior, but my perception and judgement (didn't make / didn't made) it true.
questions.analysis: 조동사 didn't 다음에는 동사원형 make가 와야 한다. didn't made는 틀린 표현.

questions.stem: 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현을 고르시오.
questions.question: There are an infinite number of examples and ways in (which / what) we judge daily.
questions.analysis: 선행사 ways가 있으므로 관계대명사 which를 사용. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 선행사 있을 때 사용 불가.

questions.stem: 다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
questions.question: One could say that judging or pre-judging are natural and necessary for protection and safety.
questions.wa: are → is (주어: judging or pre-judging은 단수 취급)
questions.analysis: 동명사 주어 judging or pre-judging은 단수 동사 is가 와야 한다.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.question: We have to ________ what type of judging we are doing — is it for safety, or are we simply making unfair assumptions about others?
questions.analysis: 본문: 'we have to distinguish what type of judging we are doing'. 구별하다(distinguish)가 정답.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.question: If we look past the surface, we may see a deeper problem that ________ some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment on our part.
questions.analysis: 본문 직접 인용: 'warrants some understanding, empathy'. warrants = 정당화하다, 필요로 하다.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.question: Judging is (A)________, but it doesn't always reflect (B)________. We must look deeper before forming conclusions.
questions.analysis: (A) 본문: 'judging or pre-judging is natural'. (B) 본문: 'my perception and judgement didn't make it true' — perception ≠ reality.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.question: The author concludes by saying that now she immediately ________ herself when she starts to judge others unfairly.
questions.analysis: 본문: 'I immediately check myself and say, "Girl, STOP!"' — check oneself = 스스로를 점검하다.

questions.stem: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸을 채워 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.question: We have to ________ what type of judging we are doing.
questions.analysis: 본문: 'we have to distinguish what type of judging we are doing'

questions.stem: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸을 채워 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.question: The author says her ________ and judgement of others didn't make it true.
questions.analysis: 본문: 'my perception and judgement didn't make it true'

questions.stem: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸을 채워 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.question: If we look past the surface, we may see a deeper problem that warrants some understanding, ________, or even enlightenment.
questions.analysis: 본문: 'warrants some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment'

questions.stem: 다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 영어 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.question: 영영풀이: to be good enough reason for something; to make something necessary or appropriate
questions.analysis: warrant = '정당화하다, ~을 필요로 하다'. 본문: 'a deeper problem that warrants some understanding'

questions.stem: 다음 우리말 뜻에 해당하는 영어 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.question: 우리말: 공감, 감정이입 (다른 사람의 감정을 이해하고 나누는 능력)
questions.analysis: 본문: 'warrants some understanding, empathy, or even enlightenment'

questions.stem: 다음 우리말 뜻에 해당하는 영어 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.question: 우리말: 인식, 지각 (현실이나 사물을 마음속에서 파악하는 방식)
questions.analysis: 본문: 'my perception and judgement didn't make it true'
